messages:
sam: quick q — our Node SDK default retry uses exponential backoff with full jitter (base=500ms, max=8s, max_retries=6). For POST endpoints and streaming uploads, should we still auto-retry if the caller didn’t provide an idempotency-key? worried about duplicate writes. also saw a burst of 429s right after an auth refresh. cc @anya @matt

anya: short answer: don’t silently retry non-idempotent POSTs. SDKs should only auto-retry safe/idempotent ops or when an explicit idempotency-key header is present. streaming uploads should expose a resume token to the app so it can decide to resume vs restart.

matt: +1 — our public clients historically default to conservative behavior. prefer: auto-retry for GET/HEAD, optional for PUT if caller opts in, require idempotency-key for POST if you want automatic retries. add a flag like `allow_non_idempotent_retries=true` for internal use only.

devx-bot: docs reference: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/retries — default policy listed: retries=3, base=500ms, cap=8000ms, jitter=full. Also: honor Retry-After header when present.

luis: for 429 specifically — always honor Retry-After if present (supports seconds or HTTP-date). if missing, fallback to exponential+full-jitter. Also, avoid retrying immediately after 401/403: try one auth refresh then retry once, otherwise surface error. that pattern prevented the token-refresh 429-loop we saw last week.

anya: streaming nuance: if connection dies mid-stream, SDK should surface a transient error + resume_token. the app can re-open the stream with resume_token and server will replay from last acked frame. never auto-retry the whole stream without explicit idempotency metadata.

sam: good. any language-specific gotchas to call out? Node/Python/Go differences?

matt: Node/Python: easy to add idempotency header helpers and a RetryPolicy class. Go: careful with goroutine leaks — ensure backoff timers are tied to request Context and that you only spawn a single retry worker per request.

luis: another gotcha: parsing Retry-After — some servers send an HTTP-date. provide helper that handles both int seconds and parseable HTTP-date fallback. include unit tests.

anya: propose doc PR: add a "retry safety" section per endpoint (safe/default/conservative), show code examples for setting idempotency-key, using Retry-After, and stream resume. also recommend full jitter for cloud-scale burst smoothing, but show how to switch to equal jitter for deterministic environments.

matt: I can own Node + Python examples. I’ll implement a small helper: `sdk.retryIfIdempotent({idempotencyKey})` plus README snippets.

luis: I’ll update runtime docs with Retry-After/401 handling and a snippet for parsing HTTP-date. will add a small integration test that simulates token refresh + 429 spike.

devx-bot: created ticket DEVEX-4781 to track README + runtime docs updates: https://issues.redwood.ai/DEVEX-4781

sam: thanks — can one of you open PRs and ping me for quick review? also, confirm we default to full jitter in released clients?

matt: yes default will be full jitter. PRs incoming from me (node/python) tomorrow. :thumbsup:

anya: I’ll draft the doc text and a short rationale paragraph about idempotency defaults.

sam: great, that should prevent more duplicate writes and the 429-after-refresh storms. thanks all.
